title: Logarithm dominated by the square
statement: As a real variable $t$ tends to $-\infty$, $\log(-t)/t^2$ tends to $0$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
replaced:
For a real variable $t$ tending to $-\infty$, with $\log$ denoting the natural logarithm, one has
\[
\lim_{t\to-\infty}\frac{\log(-t)}{t^2}=0.
\]
